questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A culture and people where I thought I would feel at home

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great but a little stressfull especially with the systems

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: As easy as any other university systems - not horrible but still a small maze

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My exchange coordinator was extremely helpful in any miscommunication and support I needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared apartments and seperate but with shared showers

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans but I had my own kitchenette

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: F building is very run down, and if you want anything done then first report it, give it max a week and then alert the one in charge of the building

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I missed an email(spam folder) and had a small issue with a course I was unable to take(but I did not know until too late in the process because of the missed email alert) but was granted permission anyway so it can be done

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get send an email with a questionnaire you fill out based on a flyer of classes you can take and a schedule module where you can check how they fit together

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: exchange coordinator was the most helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very all classes I wanted I was entered in

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check your spam folder

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Decent level difficulty overall, sometimes the form of the exams did not fit the structure of the course (multiple choice in every one, even philosophy)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was very similar, you have a lecture, you have assignments(mostly randomized groups) and some reading but you can mostly focus on the lecture

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Health economics, Urban and transport economics, Labour economics, Philosophy(for economics), Qualitative research in marketing, Seminar in health, behaviour and well-being

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are not used to not having 4 exams in one week then a course like Qualitative research in marketing is both a good way to step out of the way economics is taught and still getting something useful out of it while having one exam less as the work instead is more spread out over the block and that is what you are graded upon - overall all the courses were good and well though out

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices are very like the ones in Denmark but because of less taxing on groceries those were less expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sport which they had a good culture about, some exhibitions and stuff like that at times, a lot of social activities were tied to ESN

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went of campus and did athletics at a local club which helped a lot if you want new friends outside school and PAC Rotterdam is extremely nice and chill vibes

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Have a weekend train pass and then see the other cities, they have a good system of inter city trains - and see the foodmarkets

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a local sports club maybe outside of the campus and university life

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is not a difference but just a challenge because Im not Dutch, like Danes they do tend to go over in their own language mainly which is difficult to be a part of

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are quite active which I enjoyed

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Study from the beginning of the semester - you do not have a month to catch up before exams you have two days, throw in an easy course if you have to do 4 in one block to have the proper amount of ects, take advantage of the trains

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The systems will remind you of home you will be fine so no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends that I would want to come back to rotterdam to see

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Overlapping semesters and high workload of taking 4 courses in one block(3 is recommended but then you wont acheive the 30 ects)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
